facts.text: A digital twin is a detailed computer model of one specific real machine or site, kept matched to the real object by measurements.
facts.quote: A digital twin is a detailed computer model of one specific real machine or site, kept matched to the real thing by measurements.

facts.text: A digital twin promises agreement between the model and the specific real object, with that agreement checked using data from the real object.
facts.quote: The word "twin" promises that model and object agree, and that the agreement is checked with data from the real object.

facts.text: Machine digital twins include geometry, self-occlusion by bucket, boom or body, sensor mounting and a braking model, enabling coverage and blind zones per machine to be computed before hardware arrives.
facts.quote: For machines, it means geometry, self-occlusion by bucket, boom or body, sensor mounting and a braking model, which let coverage and blind zones per machine be computed before hardware arrives [Chapter 7].

facts.text: A cited peer-reviewed study from 2025 calibrated a wheel-loader digital twin, including soil parameters, against a physical machine.
facts.quote: One cited peer-reviewed study (2025) calibrated a wheel-loader twin, including soil parameters, against a physical machine [Chapter 11].

facts.text: Site digital twins are surveyed virtual job sites that serve as reality anchors.
facts.quote: For sites, it means surveyed virtual job sites that serve as reality anchors.

facts.text: A vendor claimed 30% faster validation cycles from a mining digital twin, but the claim concerned fleet behavior rather than perception and was not independently verified.
facts.quote: One vendor's claim of 30% faster validation cycles from a mining twin concerned fleet behavior, not perception, and was not independently verified [Chapter 1].

facts.text: Site digital twins in operating mines update at operational timescales rather than perception timescales.
facts.quote: Site twins in operating mines update "at operational timescales rather than perception timescales"

facts.text: A design model represents what was intended, whereas the brake encounters what is physically present now.
facts.quote: a design model says what was intended while the brake meets what is physically there now [Chapter 5].

facts.text: Forestry researchers argue that relying only on exact digital twins is insufficient and propose digital cousins: synthetic sites that match real-site statistics without copying the real sites.
facts.quote: Forestry researchers argue that relying only on exact twins is insufficient and propose "digital cousins", synthetic sites that match the statistics of real ones without copying them [Chapter 5].

facts.text: No credibility framework treats a digital twin as validated by name; credibility applies to a model, a configuration, a use and its evidence.
facts.quote: No credibility framework treats a twin as validated by name; credibility belongs to a model, a configuration, a use and its evidence [Chapter 10].

facts.text: Digital twins of representative machines can be built now from existing machines and re-correlated when the prototype arrives.
facts.quote: Twins of representative machines can be built now from existing machines and re-correlated when the prototype arrives

facts.text: The booklet advises against one ultimate digital twin and recommends layered models of different fidelity per machine family.
facts.quote: the booklet advises against one "ultimate" digital twin and for layered models of different fidelity per machine family [Chapter 8].
